name: SSUAS
title: Small Stealth Unmanned Aerial System
subtitle: A blended-wing-body study in low-observability aircraft design.
summary: The SSUAS project explores a compact blended-wing-body aircraft designed to reduce radar, infrared, radio-frequency and acoustic signatures. The team used House of Quality and Figure of Merit trade studies, aerodynamic and structural simulation, analytical sizing and preliminary physical prototyping to integrate the airframe, propulsion, avionics and modular payload architecture.
approach: A blended-wing-body configuration was selected to combine aerodynamic efficiency with a reduced radar signature. The intended structure uses a carbon-fiber outer skin and aluminum internal members; a full-scale MDF internal-structure model was built to check assembly. Fusion 360 structural analysis and X-band radar-cross-section estimates were used alongside performance calculations.
results: The report records a simulated safety factor of 15 and maximum displacement of 1.071 mm under the evaluated loads. Its verification table estimates radar cross-section at approximately 0.18 m², more than 99.9% below the report's raw baseline estimate. The team also built a 1:1 MDF internal-structure demonstrator. Infrared-signature reduction, collision avoidance, return-to-home behavior and yaw stability remained incomplete or required further development.
next: The report recommends further infrared testing, flight-safety functions, yaw-stability refinement and broader physical validation. The headline performance figures are simulation and analysis results, not evidence of a fully flight-tested aircraft.
caption: Full-scale MDF internal-structure demonstrator. Source: Figure 50, report page 97 (PDF page 100).
status: Integrated design, simulation and structural demonstrator

name: Mortar Glide Kit
title: A compact folding-wing glide-kit concept
subtitle: Deployable aerodynamics, guidance and structures in one compact airframe.
summary: Developed with RV CONNEX, this project studies an air-deployed glide kit for a standard 60 mm mortar round. Its engineering focus is a compact folding-wing configuration, lightweight composite structure, V-tail control, GNSS-based navigation and an integrated flight-control architecture.
approach: The final concept uses a high-mounted rectangular SD7043 wing with a 58 cm span, folding spring deployment and solenoid locking. A RAF 27 V-tail provides pitch and yaw control. The architecture combines a CUAV X7+ flight controller, GNSS, pitot-static sensing, telemetry and digital servos with CFRP plates and skins, EPS wing cores, aluminum spacers and 3D-printed ABS parts.
results: Analysis predicts approximately 35 km of glide from 4.5 km altitude, a lift-to-drag ratio near 7.8 and a total estimated mass of 2.63 kg including the 1.5 kg payload used in the final sizing. Structural analysis reports a minimum safety factor above the 3.75 requirement; the fuselage plate case is reported at 4.912. These are design and simulation results rather than demonstrated flight performance.
next: The report recommends additional finite-element work on thinner fuselage plates, alternative wing-core materials, vibration testing of the carrying mechanism and full physical and flight validation.
caption: Isometric CAD view of the integrated folding-wing concept. Source: Figure 117, report page 140 (PDF page 156).

name: Medical Delivery Drone
title: An autonomous multirotor for medical logistics
subtitle: Moving essential supplies above Bangkok traffic.
summary: The Medical Delivery Drone is a quadcopter developed to transport non-urgent medical supplies through congested urban environments. The project integrates a Pixhawk-based flight-control system, GPS navigation, automated status reporting, emergency behaviors and a dedicated medical payload box.
approach: The team selected and sized the airframe, propulsion, LiPo battery and Pixhawk-based avionics, then developed autonomous control with ArduPilot. Indoor and outdoor testing covered stability, telemetry, manual control, waypoint missions, emergency protocols and payload carriage.
results: Testing confirmed carriage of a 1.5 kg payload, endurance beyond 10 minutes, controlled manual flight to approximately 480 m and autonomous waypoint missions within a 300 m radius. During a payload flight, altitude variation remained within the report's 3 m criterion. The project notes that payload-box clearance could destabilize the aircraft after touchdown and that telemetry constrained the autonomous test radius.
next: Recommended improvements include longer-range telemetry, revised landing-gear or payload geometry and a balancing counterweight. The next validation stage should repeat autonomous payload missions after the landing interface is refined.
caption: Completed medical-delivery quadcopter. Source: Figure 13-1, report/PDF page 103.

name: SkyReach Horizon
title: A modular hybrid sounding rocket for CanSat missions
subtitle: Adjustable altitude, reusable architecture and an educational mission platform.
summary: SkyReach Horizon develops a hybrid sounding-rocket architecture for CanSat missions. The integrated design emphasizes adjustable apogee, modularity, recovery, reusable subsystems and compliance with Thai and international guidance, supported by CAD, aerodynamic and structural analysis, avionics prototyping and recovery-system tests.
approach: The team combined hybrid propulsion, a modular connector, throttle control, avionics and telemetry, staged recovery and radial CanSat deployment. CAD and ANSYS models were paired with trajectory simulation, electronics prototypes and practical recovery-sequence testing.
results: The final simulation table reports a 16,748 m apogee, Mach 1.782 maximum speed, 4.0–11.0 calibers of stability margin and 9.69 m/s ground-impact speed. The recovery sequence received practical testing, but the report states that full experimental validation of the propulsion system remained incomplete. Accordingly, the apogee and speed figures should be presented as simulated performance.
next: Priorities are propulsion testing, further prototyping of the recovery and payload-deployment mechanisms, and integrated real-world validation. The existing work provides a detailed design foundation rather than a completed launch campaign.
caption: Integrated rocket configuration and internal layout. Source: Figure 167, report/PDF page 174.
status: Integrated design, simulation and subsystem testing

name: RV Pathum 01
title: Performance evaluation and redesign of a blended-wing-body UAV
subtitle: Reworking endurance, payload and stability around an efficient flying-wing platform.
summary: Developed with RV CONNEX, this project evaluates and redesigns the RV Pathum 01 blended-wing-body UAV for medium-haul operations. The team refined the aircraft configuration, structure, propulsion, energy system and elevon controls using literature benchmarking, CAD, aerodynamic simulation and structural analysis.
approach: The redesign retains a tailless blended-wing-body layout with electric pusher propulsion and combined pitch-and-roll elevons. Eppler 355 wing sections and an Eppler 266 center section were selected, with OpenVSP/VSPAero and structural simulation used to refine aerodynamic efficiency, stability, controls and composite construction.
results: The report predicts four hours of endurance while carrying a 2 kg payload, compared with the earlier aircraft's reported 40 minutes without payload. Simulations indicate favorable lift-to-drag behavior and static stability through most of the intended envelope, while the control study identifies reduced elevon effectiveness near stall. These results are analytical and simulated; the report does not document a flight-tested redesigned aircraft.
next: The next stage should fabricate a representative airframe, validate mass and energy estimates, test the propulsion system and elevons, and conduct progressive ground and flight tests—especially around high-angle-of-attack control behavior.
caption: Top view of the redesigned blended-wing-body configuration. Source: Figure 30, report/PDF page 70.
